items.stem: A dashboard loads 50 courses and then runs one query per course to load enrolments. What is the problem and a fix?

options.text: N+1 queries; load related data with a projection or Include in a single query
options.rationale: Correct: one query per parent row is the N+1 pattern; projection/Include reduces round trips.

options.text: Too few indexes; add an index on every column
options.rationale: Indexing everything does not remove extra round trips and slows writes.

options.text: Connection pool too small; disable pooling

options.rationale: That changes test behaviour, not production queries.

items.explanation: Correct: one query per parent row is the N+1 pattern; projection/Include reduces round trips.

items.stem: Which TWO choices reduce SQL-injection risk in EF Core with MySQL? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use LINQ queries or parameterised FromSql with interpolated parameters
options.rationale: Correct: parameters keep data separate from SQL text.

options.text: Build SQL strings by concatenating user input
options.rationale: Concatenation is the classic injection vector.

options.text: Connect with a least-privilege database account
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege limits the impact of any injection.
TLS protects data in transit; disabling it adds risk.

items.explanation: Correct: parameters keep data separate from SQL text.

items.stem: Why should integration tests run against a real MySQL instance rather than EF Core's in-memory provider?

options.text: The in-memory provider does not reproduce relational behaviour such as constraints and SQL translation
options.rationale: Correct: Microsoft notes the in-memory provider is not designed for production use and may not be the best testing solution.

options.text: EF Core cannot connect to MySQL
